unit.title: Кадры в секунду и время кадра

learning_outcomes.statement: Defines FPS and frame time as reciprocals, explains that `clock.tick()` caps rather than accelerates, and introduces `clock.get_fps()` for measuring the real rate.

findings.description: S-001: «Реальный, измеренный FPS можно узнать через clock.get_fps() уже после нескольких кадров работы» understated the warm-up. Measured: get_fps() is 0.0 for ticks 1-10 and first returns a value (61.73) at tick 11; official docs confirm 'Returns 0.0 if fewer than ten ticks have been made.'
findings.resolution: Fixed in scripts/build_chapter_20.py: the vague phrase was replaced with an explicit statement that get_fps() averages the last ten tick() calls and honestly returns 0.0 until the tenth frame, plus a line telling the learner an early zero is missing statistics rather than a broken counter. Verified present in the rebuilt HTML («усредняет последние десять»).

findings.description: S-002: the vremya_kadra.py block raised NameError if pasted, since `frame_time` was used before assignment while every other python-tagged block in the chapter is runnable.
findings.resolution: Fixed in scripts/build_chapter_20.py: the block now assigns `frame_time = 1 / 60` first, derives `fps` from it, and prints both. Verified by executing the block verbatim under .venv/bin/python: it prints 0.016666666666666666 and 60.0, exactly matching its own comments, so a learner can now paste and run it.

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Defines FPS and frame time as reciprocals, explains that `clock.tick()` caps rather than accelerates, and introduces `clock.get_fps()` for measuring the real rate.
FPS and frame time are reciprocal: 60 FPS corresponds to about 16.7 ms per frame. -- Confirmed -- `1/60 = 0.016666666666666666`; the notebook prints 16.667 ms and asserts it.

`clock.tick(60)` only holds the loop back; it cannot help if one frame's own work exceeds the budget. -- Confirmed -- with 30 ms of artificial work per frame, tick(60) returns 30-31 ms and applies no delay; with no work it returns 16 ms.

`clock.get_fps()` reports the measured rate «уже после нескольких кадров». -- Was imprecise -- measured 0.0 for ticks 1-10 and 61.73 only from tick 11; official docs say 'Returns 0.0 if fewer than ten ticks have been made.' Fixed under S-001.

Without any rate limiting the loop becomes a busy loop consuming a full CPU core. -- Confirmed -- correct, and the callout properly notes other engines pace themselves differently (vsync, fixed timestep) rather than implying tick() is the only way.
